nodes.name: CC pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Before synthesis, a piece of CC (2.5 cm × 3 cm) was washed in acetone, ethanol and deionized water three times in an ultrasonic cleaner.
nodes.source_text: Before synthesis, a piece of CC (2.5 cm × 3 cm) was washed in acetone, ethanol and deionized water three times in an ultrasonic cleaner.

nodes.name: MoS2 Hydrothermal Growth
nodes.procedure: First, 0.9 mmol Na2MoO4·2H2O and 0.36 mmol CH4N2S were added to 30 mL deionized water. Then, CC was introduced into the solution, transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and maintained at 200 °C for 24 h. MoS2/CC was obtained.

nodes.procedure: Second, 0.15 mmol NiCl2·6H2O and 0.18 mmol CH4N2S were added into 30 mL deionized water. Then, the obtained MoS2/CC was immersed into the solution, transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and maintained at 180 °C for 12 h. Ni3S2/MoS2/CC was obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Ni3S2 nanoparticles modifying MoS2 nanosheets with maintained morphology and sufficient edge exposure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Comparing Fig. 1b with Fig. 1a, Ni3S2 nanoparticles modifying MoS2 nanosheets can be observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Ni3S2 nanoparticles with size of 6–22 nm on MoS2 nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni3S2 nanoparticles with a size of 6–22 nm on MoS2 nanosheets could be observed in the TEM images of Fig. 1c, d.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.244 nm and 0.282 nm for Ni3S2 (003) and (110) planes, and 0.683 nm and 0.273 nm for MoS2 (002) and (100) planes; expanded MoS2 layer spacing from 0.633 nm to 0.683 nm and creation of defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM images of Fig. 1f and Fig. 1e exhibit lattice spacings of 0.244 and 0.282 nm, respectively, belonging to the (003) and (110) crystal planes of Ni3S2 ... the larger layer spacing of MoS2 from the Ni3S2/MoS2 heterostructure (0.683 nm) compared with that from MoS2/CC (0.633 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms uniform loading of Ni3S2 nanoparticles on MoS2 nanosheets with mass fractions of 18.6% Ni3S2 and 81.4% MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping images in Fig. 1g and EDS line scanning results in Fig. S5 reveal the uniform loading of Ni3S2 nanoparticles on MoS2 nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms Ni3S2 peaks at 22°, 31.3°, 44.9° for (101), (110), (202) planes and MoS2 peaks at 13.7°, 33.2°, 39.4°, 58.6° for (002), (100), (013), (110) planes; MoS2 (002) peak shifts from 14.25° to 13.7° indicating increased interlayer spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 2a, peaks at 22, 31.3 and 44.9° should be assigned to the (101), (110) and (202) planes of Ni3S2, respectively. The peaks at 13.7, 33.2, 39.4 and 58.6° should be assigned to the (002), (100), (013), and (110) planes of MoS2, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Ni3S2 peaks at 195, 219.2, 345.5 cm⁻¹ and MoS2 E₂g¹ at 375.7 cm⁻¹, A₁g at 404.4 cm⁻¹ (redshifted from 378.3 and 405.7 cm⁻¹), confirming expanded MoS2 interlayer spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the Raman spectrum of Ni3S2/MoS2/CC in Fig. 2b, peaks at 195, 219.2, and 345.5 cm⁻¹ are the typical characteristic peaks of Ni3S2. The peaks at 375.7 and 404.4 cm⁻¹ originate from the in-plane E₂g¹ and out-of-plane A₁g vibration modes of Mo-S bonds in MoS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Mo 3d5/2 at 229.4 eV, 3d3/2 at 232.6 eV, Mo6+ at 235.8 eV; S 2p3/2 at 162.3 eV, 2p1/2 at 163.4 eV; Ni 2p3/2 peaks at 853.4 eV (Ni0), 856 eV and 857.8 eV (Ni2+, Ni3+), Ni 2p1/2 at 870.6, 873.3, 875.2 eV; increased Ni2+ and Ni3+ content and Ni 2p peak shift to higher binding energy indicating electron transfer from Ni to MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2c, peaks at 229.4 and 232.6 eV are ascribed to Mo 3d5/2 and 3d3/2, respectively. The peak at 235.8 eV could be attributed to the high oxidation state Mo6+ ... In the Ni 2p spectrum shown in Fig. 2e, peaks at 853.4, 856, and 857.8 eV are assigned to Ni 2p3/2 ... the Ni 2p peaks of Ni3S2/MoS2/CC shifted toward higher binding energy compared with Ni3S2/CC, suggesting electron migration from Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines double-layer capacitance Cdl of 40.24 mF cm⁻² for Ni3S2/MoS2/CC, 21.9 mF cm⁻² for MoS2/CC, and 0.66 mF cm⁻² for Ni3S2/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3e, the Cdl value of Ni3S2/MoS2/CC (40.24 mF cm⁻²) is almost double that of MoS2/CC (21.9 mF cm⁻²), which confirms the significant increase in active sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct of 0.66 Ω for Ni3S2/MoS2/CC, 1.63 Ω for MoS2/CC, and 68.14 Ω for Ni3S2/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EIS results (Fig. 3d), which show the much lower charge transfer resistance (Rct) of Ni3S2/MoS2/CC (0.66 Ω) than those of MoS2/CC (1.63 Ω) and Ni3S2/CC (68.14 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms no Ni or Mo leaching into KOH electrolyte after 30 h stability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Neither Ni nor Mo was detected through ICP-MS analysis of the KOH electrolyte before and after 30 h stability measurement.
